instruction: Design a single-page introduction screen for a colorful side-scrolling platform adventure inspired by classic mascot platformers. Include a bold original game title, a hero beside a layered level preview with platforms, blocks, coins, enemies, and a distant goal, plus a prominent Start Adventure button, small controls guide, world selector, and collectible counters. Put strong emphasis on a joyful original identity, clear gameplay storytelling, depth, expressive shapes, and a polished launch-screen composition.

history.critique: Brief & Intent: the explicitly required small controls guide is absent from the visible composition, and the world selector is clipped by the bottom edge, so the 'single-page launch screen' actually scrolls and terminates mid-card — a direct brief and composition failure. The hero sits small inside the level preview rather than 'beside' it as briefed, and the preview is a single flat layer (no parallax hills, no foreground grass lip, no atmospheric depth), so 'layered level preview with depth' is only nominally met. The 'distant goal' is a flag beside a generic white house that reads as a prop, not a destination. Clarity & Hierarchy: the top-right save pill says 'World 2 · 64%' while World 1 is selected and headed, creating a state contradiction; the in-preview coins render as thin yellow dashes that read as sparks rather than the coin icon used in the counters; a stray thin oval surrounds the Start button like a misdrawn focus ring, distracting from the primary CTA; and the reading flow ends abruptly on cut-off world cards. Visual System & Craft: the title is plain extra-bold system sans with a flat gray offset shadow — no outline, per-letter play, or logo treatment — so the 'bold original title' feels like default text; the UI chrome is generic dashboard (uniform rounded rectangles, hairline borders, one type family) rather than a coherent game system; the sun carries a stray stick artifact; and the world cards' star rows are clipped. Expressiveness & Distinctiveness: the identity is cute (bee, teal/yellow/coral palette) but the chrome is template-like; there is no memorable moment because the hero is small and static-feeling, the background is a flat gradient with simple mountains, and shapes are uniformly rounded with no sticker outlines, bevels, or playful rotation. Real trade-offs: (1) fitting title + hero + preview + CTA + counters + controls + world selector into one viewport forces compression — the draft chose to scroll and clipped instead of tightening; (2) moving the hero 'beside' the preview risks losing in-world storytelling — resolvable by overlapping a large hero on the preview's edge; (3) chunky game chrome can erode the clean hierarchy — resolvable by applying one consistent outline/offset-shadow system; (4) the offline constraint forbids external fonts/assets, so the logo must be crafted from system type plus CSS/SVG rather than a display font file.
history.suggestion: Priority 1 — Brief completeness and state truth: add a compact controls guide as a row of keycap chips (←/→ move, Space jump, ↓ spin) directly under the Start button or beside the counters; reconcile the save pill with the selected world (change to 'World 1 · 64%' or relabel 'Last save'); compress vertical rhythm (tighten top padding, reduce preview height ~10%, make the world selector a single compact row of four cards) so the entire launch screen fits the viewport with zero clipping. Priority 2 — Craft the title as a logo: keep the system font but treat it as display — per-letter spans with 2–4° alternating tilts, a thick dark outline via -webkit-text-stroke plus layered text-shadows for a chunky bevel, a subtle top highlight, and a small bee or honeycomb accent on one letter; this stays fully offline while making the title feel authored. Priority 3 — Rebuild the preview with depth and move the hero beside it: add three layers inside the card (distant hills + drifting clouds, mid-ground platforms/blocks, a foreground grass lip with a soft vignette), redraw coins as spinning circles matching the counter icon, and replace the house+flag with a distant castle/flag on a hill as the goal; place a large expressive Pip overlapping the preview's left edge with a gentle bob animation and grounded shadow so the hero becomes the memorable moment while the in-level scene still shows platforms, blocks, coins, enemies, and goal. Priority 4 — Unify the game UI system: give cards, chips, and the CTA a consistent 3px dark outline plus offset solid shadow (sticker style), vary radii intentionally (chunky for primary, small for chips), remove the stray oval around Start (or make it an intentional hover pulse), add hover-lift and pressed states to the CTA, fix the sun's stray stick, and add light idle motion (clouds, coin spin, hero bob) to convey joy. Priority 5 — Polish: ensure world cards show full star rows and lock states, align counter icons with in-game shapes, and verify the at-a-glance flow title → hero/preview → CTA → counters → worlds.

Brief/Intent: the hero is a giant mascot portrait inside the preview, hiding the level's start and breaking scale (the bee is larger than the goal castle), so 'a hero beside a layered level' reads as 'mascot over a level'; the copy promises 'floating islands,' 'spin through rings,' and a 'Golden Flag,' yet the preview shows a solid ground strip, no rings or springs, and a red flag on a house-like castle.
